title: Minimum Score by Changing Two Elements
summary: Given an integer array, the low score is the smallest difference between any two numbers, the high score is the largest difference, and the score is their sum.
statement: Given an integer array, the low score is the smallest difference between any two numbers, the high score is the largest difference, and the score is their sum. Change two elements to minimize the total score.
constraints: You may change exactly two array elements to arbitrary integer values.
Score is the smallest pairwise difference plus the largest pairwise difference.
hints: Sort the array; only extreme values affect the largest difference after changes.
The useful choices are changing two smallest, one smallest and one largest, or two largest values.
Compute the remaining range for each of those three cases.
Changed values can be placed inside the retained range so the minimum pairwise difference becomes zero, leaving exactly the smallest retained range.
editorial: Changed values can be placed inside the retained range so the minimum pairwise difference becomes zero, leaving exactly the smallest retained range.

tests.explanation: Changing the two extreme-impact elements leaves an optimal score three.
With three elements, two changes can make every value equal, yielding zero.
